examples.knowledge_point: Simplifying a Rational Expression Using the Pythagorean Identity
examples.worked_solution:
First, we factor the numerator:

$$
\dfrac {\cos \theta \sin^2 \theta + \cos^3 \theta} {\sin \theta}	=	\dfrac {\cos \theta \cdot (\sin^2 \theta + \cos^2 \theta)} {\sin \theta}
$$

Next, we use the Pythagorean identity to rewrite the expression in the parentheses, and then we simplify the resulting expression as much as possible.

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \cdot ({sin}^{2}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta )}{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta } & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \cdot (1)}{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta } \\  & =\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that:

$$
\dfrac {\cos \theta \sin^2 \theta + \cos^3 \theta} {\sin \theta} = \cot \theta.
$$

feedback.worked_solution:
First, we factor $\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ from the expression:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡x{cos}^{3}⁡x+{sin}^{3}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x=\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot ({cos}^{2}⁡x+{sin}^{2}⁡x)
$$

Then, we use ${cos}^{2}⁡x+{sin}^{2}⁡x=1$ to simplify the expression in the parentheses:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot ({sin}^{2}⁡x+{cos}^{2}⁡x) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot 1 \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

We conclude that

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡x{cos}^{3}⁡x+{sin}^{3}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x=\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x.
$$
